title: Permutation in String
statement: Return True if some contiguous substring of s2 is a rearrangement of s1 (same letters with the same counts). s1 has at least one character; both strings are lowercase.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(14)
    return [''.join(r.choice('abc') for _ in range(20000)), ''.join(r.choice('abc') for _ in range(40000))]

hints.1_question: Two strings are rearrangements of each other exactly when their letter counts match. What window size do you need to examine in s2?
hints.2_nudge: Slide a window of length len(s1) across s2, updating letter counts as one letter enters and one leaves.
hints.3_big_hint: Count s1 into need[26]. For each i in s2: add s2[i]; if i >= n remove s2[i-n]; if the window counts equal need, return True.

known_bugs.name: compares sets of letters instead of counts
known_bugs.followup: If s1 is 'aab', does 'abb' have the same letters with the same counts?

known_bugs.name: window never shrinks (nothing leaves)
known_bugs.followup: When the window slides one step right, what happens to the letter that falls off the left edge?

known_bugs.name: sorts every window (O(m * n log n))
known_bugs.followup: How much work does sorting each window do when s1 is 20000 characters long? Can you update counts incrementally?

followups: How would you also return the starting index of every permutation (problem 438)?
Why is comparing two 26-element arrays acceptable inside the loop?
